PullRequest.Title: fix: centre the fork tooltip on the fork button
PullRequest.Body: Fixes #335740 | Before | After | |---|---| | | | #335072 centred the fork glyph; this centres the tooltip. Three independent causes, each measured on a real hover in a running build. **1. The separator inflated the hover target — `chat.css`, −3.8px** The `·` was an in-flow `::before` on `.chat-fork-action-item`, so the managed hover anchored to a box spanning `dot + 4px gap + button`. It now draws in the item's left gutter (`position: absolute; right: 100%`, gutter reserved with `margin-left`), leaving the item's border box equal to the button — hover target width 36.71px → 29.14px, net layout shift **+0.44px**. `pointer-events: none` also makes the dot inert; it was previously a click target for Fork. **2. Caret rounding on odd tooltip widths — `hoverWidget.ts`, +0.5px** The hover is positioned unrounded (`target.center.x - clientWidth / 2`) but the caret was placed at `Math.round(hoverWidth / 2)`. Since `_x` is itself fractional, that rounding could never snap the caret to a device pixel — it only broke the centring. Removed on both axes. **3. Caret half-width vs `PointerSize` under zoom — `hover.css`, −0.25px** `PointerSize` (3) is treated as the caret's half-width, but its `1px` borders round down to whole device pixels under zoom, leaving a 5.86px box centred at 2.93px. Sizing it as a `border-box` 6px square keeps the centre at exactly `PointerSize` at any zoom. The `.locked` variant drops its `width/height: 4px` (which would now mean a 4px *border* box) and is visually unchanged. ### Verification Measured against each hover's real anchor element, every pointer tooltip now centres within **0.011px**, independent of width parity and zoom. Before: odd-width tooltips +0.5px, fork button −3.78px. Note: several controls anchor their hover to a parent rather than the visible `.action-label` (Toggle Chat uses `DIV.action-container`), so measuring the inner element reports a spurious ~0.5px. ### Tests `chatForkActionViewItem.test.ts` gains a case rendering the fork item as a **non-first** toolbar item so `:not(:first-child)` applies, asserting the item's box equals the button's box and the separator is out of flow and not hit-testable. Verified it fails on the pre-fix CSS. 193 passing across the fork and hover suites; `hygiene` and `stylelint` clean.

Scenarios.Scenario: Displaying or relaying out a workbench hover with a pointer, including initial show, dynamic markdown/HTML resize, and persistent-hover window resize
Scenarios.CriticalPath: HoverWidget.render/layout synchronously reads target and hover geometry, computes placement, writes pointer classes/styles, and updates contents before the tooltip is positioned. The diff only replaces Math.round(width-or-height / 2) with the unrounded division and changes static caret box geometry; it adds no geometry read, extra layout pass, or deferred work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One layout per shown hover plus content/resize-driven relayouts; targetElements controls bounding-rect multiplicity. The changed arithmetic remains O(1) per layout and does not alter effective hover-stack cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All geometry/style work remains serialized on the browser UI thread. ResizeObserver, async markdown callbacks, and sticky-hover resize handlers retain their prior scheduling; the diff adds no queue, burst, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No placement cache exists or is invalidated by the change; cold and warm hover layouts perform the same pre-existing measurements. Static CSS applies once per pointer element.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed hunk and layout call path show identical read/write cardinality and only cheaper/equivalent arithmetic plus a 6px border-box replacing the prior bordered content box.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hover frequency and content-resize frequency vary by feature, but there is no changed performance mechanism whose magnitude needs estimation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Pointer centering changes values only; synchronous layout work, DOM cardinality, event scheduling, and rendering scope are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering and hovering the Fork control in a visible chat checkpoint toolbar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A virtualized WorkbenchObjectTree row renders/reuses its checkpoint toolbar, refreshes menu actions, and the browser performs style/layout for the existing fork-item pseudo-element. Hovering the button then enters the unchanged managed-hover path. The diff moves the existing separator pseudo-element out of flow and reserves the same gutter with margin; it creates no DOM node or JavaScript layout read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one fork separator per rendered eligible request row, bounded in practice by virtualized visible rows rather than full conversation history. Effective pseudo-element cardinality is unchanged from before the PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Row rendering, toolbar refresh, style calculation, and hover handling remain serialized on the UI thread. No changed listener, observer, batching, or asynchronous work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat tree templates are reused for virtualized rows; the diff does not change template ownership, menus, hover caching, or invalidation. Cold and reused-row behavior have the same element/pseudo-element count.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer and disposal paths establish virtualized rows, while the CSS diff preserves one ::before per eligible item and substitutes absolute positioning/margin for in-flow gap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Conversation length and visible-row count vary, but the unchanged pseudo-element cardinality and absence of added layout reads make a material regression implausible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The CSS changes separator geometry without adding repeated work, retained state, DOM nodes, or a new rendering boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Clicking the Fork button after locating it via its tooltip
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A genuine button click runs ForkConversationAction. Native sessions synchronously serialize/clone history up to the selected request before opening the new session; contributed sessions await one provider fork and then open the result. The CSS change does not alter button invocation, and pointer-events:none prevents the separator gutter from invoking the action rather than adding calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and deep-clone chat session data, truncate to the fork point, and regenerate request identifiers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per native fork invocation, processing requests through the selected fork point
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serialization and cloning ran for clicks on the fork control before this CSS/hover change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks creation/loading of the forked model before navigation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the contributed chat session's forkSession provider callback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per unique source session/request while in flight; duplicate concurrent invocations are coalesced by ForkConversationAction.pendingFork
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The provider call and pending-request coalescing were unchanged; the new inert separator can only remove accidental invocations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the forked session can be opened

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Native clone cost scales with session requests up to the fork point. Contributed forking is one provider call per unique session/request key, with concurrent duplicates coalesced by pendingFork. Neither scaling relationship is increased by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Native cloning remains one synchronous action execution. Contributed provider calls retain pendingFork coalescing by source/request, and session opening remains sequenced after successful fork.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is added or bypassed. Existing open-session reveal behavior and pendingFork in-flight coalescing remain unchanged; warm already-open handling is unaffected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the click target CSS, action call path, native clone, and contributed-provider coalescing are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session history size and provider latency vary, but those costs are pre-existing and the diff cannot increase their invocation cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. All expensive fork boundaries are pre-existing and unchanged for button clicks, while separator clicks are eliminated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and all diff pages. Traced hover layout/rendering, virtualized checkpoint toolbar rendering, and the fork action's serialization/provider boundaries. The PR changes only pointer geometry and separator hitbox/layout values; it adds no hot-path work, fan-out, retention, concurrency, or boundary calls, so no findings were submitted.
